title: Alcoholic
alt: Two-panel comic. A man turns the phrase ‘could be’ into ‘cold beer,’ then has a revelation and declares, ‘That’s it! I’m an alcoholic!’
description: A two-panel wordplay comic about turning ‘could be’ into ‘cold beer’ and reaching an unfortunate revelation.
transcript: Panel 1: A tired-looking man sits at a table beside a mug. He says, ‘Could be.’ In a thought bubble, he repeats the phrase and gradually changes it: ‘Could be… cold be… cold beer…’
Panel 2: A light bulb appears above the man's head. He raises one finger with a startled expression and declares, ‘That's it! I'm an alcoholic!’

title: Douchebag
alt: Two-panel comic. A man celebrates winning an online chess game, then says, ‘Yeah, they should have stuck to medicine!’
description: A two-panel online-chess comic about beating a player named Dr.MateMD and drawing a smug conclusion.
transcript: Panel 1: A man sits at a computer after an online chess game. The screen shows that pawgniid defeated Dr.MateMD, whose rating is 1827, and displays ‘You won.’ The man celebrates: ‘Yes!’
Panel 2: The man turns away from the computer with a smug expression, raises one finger, and says, ‘Yeah, they should have stuck to medicine!’

title: Fool
alt: A tired-looking man wonders, ‘Why?? Why can’t I find the energy?’ while vaping from a device labeled ‘Juulfool.’
description: A tired man wonders why he cannot find any energy while vaping from a device labeled Juulfool.
transcript: Single panel: An exhausted-looking man with heavy eyelids inhales from a teal vaping device while a cloud of vapor drifts behind him. He thinks, ‘Why?? Why can't I find the energy?’
The vaping device in his hand is labeled ‘Juulfool.’

title: Artist
alt: A comic artist condemns AI-generated art, briefly imagines using it to finish work and spend time with family, dismisses the idea as bullshit, then resumes drawing alone late at night.
description: A comic artist condemns AI-generated art, imagines using it to finish work and spend time with family, then returns to drawing alone.
transcript: Panel 1: A furious comic artist gestures with both hands and shouts, ‘AI-generated art is destroying my livelihood!!’
Panel 2: His expression softens as he considers another possibility: ‘But wait… am I wrong?’
Thought sequence, panel 1: He photographs a drawing of a knight facing a dragon.
Thought sequence, panel 2: At a computer, he enters the prompt ‘Draw knight entering town in style of photo’ and selects ‘Generate.’
Thought sequence, panel 3: He looks at the generated image of a knight riding through a town.
Thought sequence, panel 4: He happily spends time playing a board game with his family.
Panel 3: He dismisses the idea, thinking, ‘Nah never mind—that's bullshit!’
Panel 4: Late at night, he sits alone at his desk and continues drawing by hand.
caption: Turns out the process described in the thought bubble doesn't work as reliably as I thought. I'm not going to remove this comic because my mistake is funny. In my defense, an LLM *did* make comic #3 based on the style of #2.

title: Moderators
alt: Four-panel comic. A post arguing about freelance-platform fees is automatically removed for containing an external link. The author politely messages the moderators, then is temporarily banned for self-promotion.
description: A comic about an automatically removed Reddit post, a polite appeal to moderators, and a five-day ban for self-promotion.
transcript: Panel 1: A Reddit-style post is being submitted to r/Fiverr. It reads, ‘Freelance platforms like Fiverr and Upwork might be bad for the economy because of their fees. A privately owned, publicly owned, nonprofit, taxpayer-funded, or otherwise public-interest alternative could provide the same marketplace function without taking a cut from transactions. But I defer to the expert consensus on this one.’ An external link follows. The cursor clicks ‘Post.’
Panel 2: A red X appears above the notice ‘Post removed automatically.’ The reason given is: ‘External links can be self-promotion.’
Panel 3: The author writes to the r/Fiverr moderators: ‘I hope you're having a great day! Please allow the post. It doesn't count as self-promotion.’ The cursor clicks ‘Send.’
Panel 4, labeled ‘A day or two later’: A notice says, ‘You have been temporarily banned from participating in r/Fiverr for 5 days.’ The moderator note reads, ‘Rule 1: No self-promotion.’

title: Executive
alt: A pharmaceutical chemist earning $78,000 says it is okay that India copied a drug formula because people need it. A pharmaceutical executive earning $363,000 angrily protests the cost of research and development and India's lack of respect for intellectual property. A closing line says the executive believes his higher pay reflects higher aptitude, a larger skillset, and a properly oriented moral compass.
description: A pharmaceutical chemist and executive take opposing positions on drug formulas, intellectual property, research costs, and access to medicine.
transcript: Left side: A calm pharmaceutical chemist wearing glasses and a lab coat is labeled ‘$78,000/year.’ She says, ‘I think it's okay that India copied the formula. Their people need—’

Right side: A pharmaceutical executive in a suit points at her and shouts. He is labeled ‘$363,000/year’ and says, ‘Do you have any idea how much R&D costs?! India has no respect for innovation or intellectual property!!’ The word ‘property’ is underlined.
Closing caption: ‘The pharmaceutical executive believes his higher pay reflects higher aptitude, a larger skillset, and a properly oriented moral compass.’

title: American
alt: A red-eyed American software engineer wearing a Make America Great Again hat smokes a joint while working from home and declaring that only Americans should do online work for American companies.
description: A political workplace comic about a marijuana-smoking American remote software engineer who argues that only Americans should do online work for American companies.

authorNote.intro: I posted this comic on Imgur and received some backlash. Since its target was not clear to everyone, here is the context I intended.
authorNote.html:
The character is deliberately offensive. I believe I have standing to draw these traits because they overlap with my own: I use marijuana and am trying to quit because I believe it makes me stupid; I am an American citizen and a coder; I have a bad back and forward-head posture; and I am skinny. I am not, however, a Republican, and I do not want to deprive other people of work. That is the difference between me and the character.

The comic’s actual subject is labor. In my view, the American middle class is waging class warfare against competent foreign workers by barring their entry into skilled jobs. A person of sound body and mind should have the opportunity to work for cheap when advancement within the company is not merely possible, but easy. For many of us, there is no other way in. Many people begin at low pay, gain experience, and later become more successful within the same company.

I also believe that barring skilled workers from the American labor force is a form of rent-seeking. Wikipedia gives this example:

Another example of rent-seeking is the limiting of access to lucrative occupations, as by medieval guilds or modern state certifications and occupational licensing.

I believe middle-class Americans—particularly people like the character in this comic—are directly responsible for this behavior. Artificially limiting the labor supply to raise the price of labor while avoiding harder work is exactly the kind of conduct this comic is intended to ridicule.

transcript: Single panel: The heading reads, ‘The American software engineer.’ A subheading says, ‘He works at home. He makes $70K/year.’
A red-eyed man sits at a table typing on a laptop while smoking a joint. He wears a red ‘Make America Great Again’ hat, a blue hoodie, and a gold dollar-sign necklace.
The software engineer says, ‘Only Americans should do online work for American companies.’
